chunks: 1- Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Ibn al-Mughirah, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
When a man performs wudu (ablution), let him splash his face with water, for if he is drowsy he will be startled and awaken, and if it is cold he will be startled and not feel the cold.
2- As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from his father, from Ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
Do not strike your faces with water when you perform wudu (ablution), but rather pour the water gently.

So the way to reconcile the two is that one of them is understood as recommendation and desirability, and the other as permissibility, and a person has the choice in acting according to either of them.

key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, the part being washed in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How are hadiths about splashing or gently pouring water on the face during wudu (ablution) reconciled?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the manner of washing the face during wudu (ablution). One report permits splashing the face with water for practical benefit, while another discourages striking the face and recommends pouring the water gently; the reconciliation given is that one indicates recommendation and the other permissibility.
